summary: Julia Ching was a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the College of New Rochelle (~1954–1958), the Catholic University of America (~1965–1966), and the Australian National University (~1968–1971), later holding a post at the University of Toronto (~1978–2001).

Sinologist and art historian Julia F. Andrews studied at Brown University (1970–1974), UC Berkeley (1976–1977), and Harvard University (1977–1984). She held a post at Ohio State University around 1987 and taught Sarah Aoife Richardson.
Julia Leslie worked in indology and religious studies. She founded SOAS University of London and held an academic post there from around 1995 to 2004.

Julian Strube specializes in religious studies and indology. He studied at Heidelberg University (2005–2015, 2020) and the University of Amsterdam (2009–2010), holding posts at Heidelberg (2015–2019), Amsterdam (2016–2017), the University of Münster (2019–2021), and the University of Vienna (~2021).

Juliane Schober works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989, taught Brooke Schedneck, and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University (attested 2007).

Julie A. Gifford is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Frank E. Reynolds and held a post at Miami University.

Indologist Julius Eggeling studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber. He served as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1869–1875) and Professor at University College London and the University of Edinburgh (~1875–1914).

Julius Euting was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. After studying at the University of Tübingen (~1857–1861) under Rudolf von Roth, he held positions at the Bibliothèque nationale et universitaire de Strasbourg (~1871–1909) and the University of Strasbourg (~1880–1909).

Julius Grill, an indologist and religious studies scholar, studied at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and Adalbert Kuhn. He served as Professor at the University of Tübingen (1888) and at the Evangelical Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren (~1888–1908).

Indologist and linguist Julius Jolly studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber and with Martin Haug. From around 1872 to 1923, he held posts at the University of Würzburg, serving as Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology from ~1877.

Julius Lipner specializes in indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at King's College London, the University of Birmingham (~1971–1974), and Clare Hall, Cambridge, later holding posts at Birmingham (~1973–1975) and the University of Cambridge (~1975). He taught Jacqueline Suthren Hirst.
Jun Fujii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~2000–2005) and held a post as a full-time lecturer at Komazawa University around 2010.

Indologist and religious studies scholar Jun Takashima studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara and at Kyoto University. He held positions at JSPS (~1988–1990), Aichi Prefectural University (~1990–1993), and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2000–2021).

Jundo Nagashima is an indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University and the University of Bristol (PhD attested 2002) under Paul Williams, Alexis Sanderson, and Seitatsu Matsunami. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2006–2017).

June McDaniel is a scholar of indology and religious studies who earned degrees from Emory University and the University of Chicago. She held posts in philosophy and religious studies at the College of Charleston, attested in 2000 and 2015.

Junglan Bang specializes in indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Dongguk University under Seung-suk Jung and Sungdoo Ahn, earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg (2012) under Harunaga Isaacson, and served as a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

Jungmin Ha works in history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She earned a master's degree at Seoul National University under Juhyung Rhi and a PhD at Duke University (attested 2016) under the supervision of Stanley Abe.

Buddhist studies and indology scholar Junjirō Takakusu studied at Ryukoku, Tokyo, and Oxford universities under Max Müller, Sylvain Lévi, and Moriz Winternitz. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1897–1927) and founded Osaka University of Foreign Studies.
Junkei Washio was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Toyo University (~1890–1893) and held posts at the Sendan-Rin School, Toyo University, and Komazawa University (~1925).

Indology and Buddhist studies scholar Junkichi Imanishi studied at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1963). He held posts at Hokkaido University (~1968–1996), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2014), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~2005–2011).
